sections.what: Daya supports South Asian survivors of domestic and sexual violence in the Houston region. It combines confidential crisis support, licensed counseling, housing assistance and economic empowerment. Culturally specific advocacy and legal referrals help survivors pursue safety and practical stability.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 annual report reports 683 clients, including 75 counseling, 75 supportive housing and 109 economic empowerment users. Crisis and legal referrals overlap these groups. These are service outputs, not measured causal improvement. Reported counties imply 87% Houston MSA share. Obtain deduplicated households, completed dose, net assistance and earnings after alternatives, and safety/privacy outcomes.
sections.qualitative: Culturally specific support addresses language and access barriers. Dated counseling and practical-support outputs expose distinct mechanisms. Original returns reveal full event costs and three comparable expense years. Overlapping clients are not confirmed unique households or causal beneficiaries. Net earnings, durable safety and household assistance additionality are unmeasured. Latest available costs and newer outputs cover different fiscal years; next-gift capacity is unknown. Official homepage and original IRS returns identify Daya Inc, EIN 76-0513273. Its current linked Qgiv route was checked without a transaction. Legal referral is not equivalent to direct representation by staff attorneys.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $265.40 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 0.076447 clinical QALYs and -0.003090 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.000377 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $1,946,855. 683 broad clients times judged .8 distinct-household share and .35 incremental annual response define the exposed union. A 75-person counseling subgroup, not additional population, receives judged .35 improvement, .05 utility for half a year. Safety/privacy harm .0005 applies fully to all exposed households. Independent .25 resource success receives $300 net work resources after taxes, childcare, commute and foregone earnings plus $500 usable assistance after alternative aid and benefit withdrawal. These are hypotheses, not gross grant receipts. Each positive component is reduced by overlap .5; full $100 attendance, safety and opportunity burden remains on all households. Union 191.23999999999998 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 7.35; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Assistance is a transfer, not automatically new social income. Distinct taxpayer or displaced-beneficiary incidence and provider opportunity costs are tested separately; recipient grants already in the annual denominator are not charged twice. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY2024 $1,928,451 tax expenses plus $18,404 netted direct event cost gives $1,946,855. FY2023 $1,694,184 plus $18,861 gives $1,713,045; FY2022 $1,417,570 plus $16,537 gives $1,434,107. Schedule D reconciles expense totals without a populated additional donated-resource adjustment. This is not evidence that volunteer resources cost zero. Newer FY2025 outputs versus FY2024 cost are a conditional scope mismatch. Reserves do not demonstrate an expansion bottleneck.

model.costScope: Whole annual recognized recipient cost versus narrow counseling and practical-resource channels; other portfolio and next gift unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Reported 2025 county shares imply .87 Houston MSA; applied once
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Other victim services, public benefits, legal aid, family support and employment alternatives retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional survivor safety and trauma recovery, usable assistance and net work resources; not calls, referrals or gross grants
